text:
grace: Heads-up — I'm putting together packaging/naming guidelines for quant profiles so Redwood Optimize can recommend them and users can roll them out reliably. Need quick alignment before I write the doc.

maya: +1. We should decide both the on-disk artifact layout and the visible name schema in the UI.

sahil: For artifact: qpkg tarball with a tiny manifest.json and a profiles/ dir. Keep it explicit so CI can validate. Example manifest I like: 
```
{
  "qprofile_name": "awq-int8-64k-v1",
  "model_family": "gpt-4o-mini",
  "backend": "awq",
  "precision": "int8",
  "max_seq": "64k",
  "accuracy_delta": "-0.6%",
  "benchmark_hash": "sha256:..."
}
```
This lets Optimize surface compat and perf tradeoffs.

tom: naming nit: avoid embedding too many knobs in the canonical name — use labels/tags in manifest for extras (e.g. tokenizer quirks, KV-layout). Keep name short + semantic version. e.g. `gpt4o-mini-awq-int8@v1` or `awq/int8@gpt4o-mini@v1`.

eva: Also need compatibility matrix fields: quant backend -> runtime kernel requirements (e.g., `requires_fp8_kernel: false`, `requires_awq_kernels: true`) so Dedicated/private deployments can validate ahead-of-time.

maya: On the Optimize side, we should expose three channels per profile: `recommended`, `canary`, `legacy`. Users can pick channel; recommended updates when accuracy/regressions are within thresholds.

grace: On accuracy delta reporting — prefer relative token-level LLM evals across our standard suite (SQuAD-ish, hallucination probes, instruction-compliance). Put summary in manifest as `eval_summary` with short IDs + deltas. Avoid raw large eval blobs in the qpkg.

ci-bot: validation: qpkg schema check passed for `awq-int8-64k-v1` (sha256:abc123). Missing `kernel_requirements` field flagged as warning.

sahil: For versioning, semver-ish `v1`, `v1.1` for micro changes (calibration/solver hyperparams), and `v2` for different quant algorithm (GPTQ -> AWQ change). Keep migration rules in manifest: `migration_notes` and `fallback_profile` fields.

tom: Packaging detail: include a `compatibility.json` that lists supported model checkpoints (hashes + names) and tokenizer versions. We ran into tokenization drift with gpt-style families in earlier bakeoffs.

maya: UI concern — users search profiles by simple facets: backend, precision, seq_len, model_family, accuracy_delta_range. Manifest keys should be normalized snake_case.

grace: Good call. Also, for Optimize suggestions, we want to attach a `suggestion_reason` and `cost_delta_estimate` to each profile so recommendations are explainable: e.g. `cost_delta_estimate: -18%`, `reason: batching-friendly, low kv memory`.

eva: For safety/regression guarding, add `eval_anchor_hash` that references the eval set used and `regression_threshold` (e.g., 1.0% absolute). If a new profile breaches that threshold, Optimize should mark it `unsafe_for_production`.

sahil: Operationally, qpkg naming in registries: consider namespaced ids like `redwood/qprof/gpt4o-mini/awq-int8@v1` for global registry + `org/foo/qprof/...` for private registries.

grace: Action items: 
- maya: draft the manifest schema with required vs optional fields (deadline Wed EOD).
- tom: write the compatibility.json example and tokenization notes (Thu).
- sahil: add CI validation rules + fallback/migration checks (Thu).
- eva: add runtime kernel flag list and regression policy text (Fri).
- i'll consolidate into a short spec for the docs site once we have the schema.

maya: I'll prototype the manifest and push a sample qpkg to the staging registry; will ping this thread.

ci-bot: deploy: staging registry upload succeeded for `redwood/qprof/gpt4o-mini/awq-int8@v1` (sha256:abc123) — visibility: engineers-only.

sahil: One more UX thought — expose `human_name` and `short_description` in manifest so Optimize UI can show friendlier text instead of raw tags.

grace: Love it. If nobody objects I’ll incorporate these points and open a PR with the schema + one real example qpkg. Thanks all. :rocket:
